districts.notes: Largest district; capital of the governorate. A 2025 academic paper on the district's units lists 7 entries (omitting Altun Kupri), but the COSIT-based 2024 census arithmetic (district total 1,549,454 vs. the other 7 subdistricts) and en.wikipedia's Altun Kupri article (infobox: District = Kirkuk) confirm Altun Kupri as the 8th subdistrict of Kirkuk District.

ar.wikipedia's قضاء الدبس article claims a 'ناحية القدس' follows the district, but this is unverified and contradicted by the 2024 census data (Dibis 54,614 + Sargaran 23,487 = 78,101 = full district total); ناحية القدس is therefore excluded. Kurdish name uncertain: ar.wikipedia's district article gives پردێ (which is actually Altun Kupri's Kurdish name) while its town article gives دووبز; left empty.

Subdistrict list confirmed via COSIT/citypopulation 2018 estimates: Daquq district total 95,109 = Dāqūq 66,433 + Ar-Rashād 28,676. ar.wikipedia's قضاء داقوق article lists only مقاطعات (land parcels), not nahiyas, and loosely describes ناحية الرشاد as bordering the district to the east; the COSIT sums are the authoritative placement of Ar-Rashad in Daquq District.

Subdistrict list confirmed via COSIT/citypopulation 2018 estimates: Hawija district total 293,290 = Al-Ḥawījah 120,679 + Al-'Abāsī 54,526 + Ar-Riyāḍ 60,499 + Az-Zāb 57,586; also consistent with ar.wikipedia's قضاء الحويجة article listing الحويجة، الزاب، العباسي، الرياض among its towns. A motion was submitted by Kirkuk provincial council members to make Hawija a separate governorate (ar.wikipedia, citing archived source).

provinces.notes: Kirkuk Governorate (محافظة كركوك, IQ-KI) is the centerpiece of the disputed territories of northern Iraq under Article 140 of the Iraqi Constitution; its final status (whether it joins the Kurdistan Region) remains unresolved. It has 4 districts and 16 subdistricts (نواحي) per the official COSIT structure used in the 2024 census (population 2,034,627). Altun Kupri town is additionally described as disputed in its own right.

provinces.notes: DISCREPANCIES: (1) en.wikipedia 'Districts of Iraq' lists 10 qada'a for Baghdad (used here as the official structure): Abu Ghraib, Al-Adhamiyah, Al-Karkh, Kadhimiya, Al-Mada'in, Mahmudiya, Al-Rasafa, Sadr City 1, Sadr City 2, Al Tarmia. (2) The en.wiki 'Baghdad Governorate' article instead lists 10 MUNICIPAL/Amanat units (Adhamiyah, Karkh, Karrada, Kadhimiya, Mansour, Sadr City, Al-Rashid, Al-Rusafa, New Baghdad, Al-Ghazaliya) — these are the 2003-era city kati'/district advisory councils under Amanat Baghdad, not qada'a; Karrada, Mansour, New Baghdad, Al-Rashid, Al-Ghazaliya are not qada'a. (3) ar.wikipedia 'أقضية العراق' lists 14 qada'a (adds Sha'ab, Al-Husayniyah (created 2013), Az-Zawra' (created 2018), Ash-Sha'lah) — newer official splits not yet reflected on en.wiki. (4) citypopulation.de's 2024-census update shows a newer COSIT reorganization: Az-Zahur, Ar-Rashidiyah, Az-Zawra', Fada' al-Kadhimiyah (At-Taji), and Sama al-Kadhimiyah (Dhat as-Salasil) now appear as separate districts; this dataset keeps the established 10-district structure. Subdistrict groupings per district were taken from citypopulation.de district pages (COSIT data); Wikipedia's own district articles do not list nahiya. Arabic spellings normalized to standard Arabic orthography.

provinces.notes: Official district count is disputed. en.wikipedia 'Districts of Iraq' lists 8 districts; ar.wikipedia (محافظة الأنبار, أقضية العراق) and the official-statistics-based 'قائمة نواحي العراق' show 10-11. The 3 newer districts included here: (1) Al-Amiriyah (العامرية) - appears as a district in the official subdistrict list; formerly a nahiya of Fallujah. (2) Khalidiya - this is the district listed by citypopulation.de, IOM DTM, and Iraqi statistics; officially قضاء الحبانية (Al-Habbaniyah District) centered on Al-Khalidiya city, and Iraqi media call it قضاء الخالدية with its own qaimmaqam. (3) Al-Karmah (الكرمة) - ar.wiki's Fallujah article (citing a 2026 academic study of administrative changes) says it is now a district with nawahi Al-Khayrat and Al-Jazira, though the official subdistrict list still places ناحية الكرمة under Fallujah. EXCLUDED (insufficient corroboration): قضاء الصقلاوية (2017 Anbar provincial-council vote to elevate Saqlawiyah nahiya; still listed as a Fallujah nahiya officially) and قضاء الرمانة (3 Sept 2019 provincial-council vote to elevate ناحية العبور/الرمانة; still listed as ناحية العبور under Al-Qa'im officially). Haditha is currently its own district; older sources placing Haditha under Anah District are outdated. No Kurdish names are in use in Anbar (Sunni Arab-majority governorate).

provinces.notes: District list follows the most current official scheme (11 districts) per citypopulation.de's 2024-census data and the ar.wiki 'أقضية العراق' list (10; missing only Aṣ-Ṣādiq). English Wikipedia's Basra Governorate article is outdated: it lists only 8 districts (missing Al-Haritha, As-Sadiq, Safwan) and ar.wiki's محافظة البصرة article still lists 9. Subdistricts verified from current ar.wiki district articles and confirmed where possible: As-Siba (Abu Al-Khaseeb), At-Tanuma/Al-Fayha/An-Nashwa/Al-Kabasi/Ataba (Shatt Al-Arab), Al-Imam Al-Qaim (Al-Qurna), Izz ad-Din Salim (Al-Midaina), Umm Qasr + Khor Az-Zubayr (Al-Zubair), Al-Faw + Al-Bihar + Al-Khalij Al-Arabi (Al-Faw). Official stats (citypopulation.de subdistrict table, still the older scheme) agree on As-Siba, An-Nashwa, Ath-Thughir (=Al-Imam Al-Qaim), Izz ad-Din Salim and Umm Qasr, but do not track the newer subdistricts (Khor Az-Zubayr, Al-Fayha, At-Tanuma, Al-Kabasi, Ataba) nor the Faw subdistricts البحار/الخليج العربي — possible lag in official data; flagged per district.

provinces.notes: Nineveh comprises nine districts in the federal Iraqi listing; Aqrah (Akre), formerly a tenth district, is now officially in Dohuk Governorate and is excluded. Several districts lie in the disputed territories: Makhmur is claimed by the KRG (Erbil) but administered by Baghdad as part of Nineveh since 2017, and Sinjar, Shekhan, Tel Afar and the Nineveh Plains districts (Al-Hamdaniya, Tel Keppe) are disputed areas with de facto KRG/Dohuk administration over parts (notably northern Shekhan). citypopulation.de lists a Faidah (فايدة) subdistrict under Nineveh, but official district totals do not allocate it to any Nineveh district; ar.wikipedia places ناحية فايدة in Sumel district, Dohuk, so it is excluded here.

provinces.notes: Current official structure is 13 districts + 3 subdistricts (16 units), per citypopulation.de Iraq admin page (2024 census data) and a 2026 University of Al-Qadisiyah journal paper (مجلة القادسية للعلوم الإنسانية), which explicitly assigns the only remaining subdistricts: Nafar (Afaq district), Al-Salahiyah (Shamiya), Al-Bassamiya (Hamza). Recent Iraqi news corroborates district status for Shanafiya, Sudayr, Shafi'iyah, Al-Budair, and Hamza Al-Sharqi. Older sources (ar.wikipedia governorate article — still not updated; en.wikipedia 'Districts of Iraq'; IOM 2009 profile) list only 4 districts (Diwaniya, Al-Shamiya, Afaq, Hamza) with 11 subdistricts — the other 9 districts are former subdistricts that were upgraded. Discrepancies: (1) citypopulation.de lists the Daghara district as 'Akad [Ad-Daghārah]' (native اكد) — uncorroborated anywhere else, so الدغارة retained; (2) ar.wikipedia's قضاء الحمزة article title uses 'Al-Hamza' but its text and 2025 Iraqi news use the official name الحمزة الشرقي (Hamza Al-Sharqi); (3) Al-Budair is also written آل بدير. kur fields intentionally empty — no Kurdish names used for this governorate.

Elevated from a nahiya of Amara district to a district in 2018 (governor's office announcement; confirmed by citypopulation.de 2024 census district table and ar.wikipedia). Internal nahiya structure unverified; only the district center is listed.

provinces.notes: District count discrepancy: English Wikipedia ('Maysan Governorate', 'Districts of Iraq') lists 6 districts, but citypopulation.de's admin table (2024 census), ar.wikipedia's Kumayt article, and the 2018 Maysan governor's office announcement all confirm Kumayt (كميت) was elevated from a nahiya of Amara district to its own district (قضاء كميت), giving 7 districts. Using the most current (7-district) list. Subdistrict Arabic spellings verified against ar.wikipedia 'قائمة نواحي العراق'. Subdistrict lists include the district center (مركز قضاء), which official Iraqi stats count as a second-level unit alongside nahiyas; 8 nahiyas proper + 7 centers = 15 entries. In 2018 Maysan also created two new nahiyas (البتيرة، نهر سعد) but no source I could access places them under a specific district, so they are omitted. Kumayt's internal nahiya structure could not be verified (only its center is listed).

districts.notes: Provincial capital. Its former subdistricts al-Batha'a (2019), Sayyid Dakhil (2018) and al-Islah (2014) were elevated to districts; only Nahiya Ur remains (confirmed by al-Batha'a's 2019 border description: 'nahiya Ur in Qada'a al-Nasiriyah').
All four of its former subdistricts — al-Dawaya, al-Gharraf, al-Nasr and al-Fajr — have been elevated to districts (2018–2019); only the district centre remains.
Its former subdistricts Qal'at Sukkar (2018), al-Nasr (2018) and al-Fajr (2019) are now separate districts; only the district centre remains.

Nahiya al-Tar was transferred to the new Karmat Bani Sa'id District and Karmat Bani Sa'id itself became a district (2019). A Qada'a al-Ukaikah was proposed in 2019 but its approval could not be confirmed.

Nahiya al-Fuhud was elevated to a district (Sept 2018); one academic paper (~2024) still lists al-Fuhud under al-Jibayish — outdated. Older COSIT data also listed a Nahiya al-Hamar; the current (2022) admin table lists Nahiya al-Manar.

Elevated from nahiya of Nasiriyah to district in 2014; confirmed in the 2018 IHEC/Ministry of Planning 10-district list. Omitted from the current ar.wikipedia 'Aqdia al-Iraq' list (likely incompleteness).

Elevated from nahiya of Nasiriyah to district (2018 wave, named in the IHEC director's official list); the governorate's official site (2026) still treats it as a qada'a. Omitted from the current ar.wikipedia 'Aqdia al-Iraq' list.
Elevated from nahiya of al-Rifa'i to district (2018 wave).
Elevated from nahiya of Shatrah to district (2018 wave).
Elevated from nahiya of Shatrah to district (2018 wave; named in the IHEC director's official list).

Elevated from nahiya of al-Jibayish to district, Sept 2018 (cited as source by ar.wikipedia); listed as a district by COSIT/citypopulation and in 2026 press. One ~2024 academic paper still calls it a nahiya of al-Jibayish.
Elevated from nahiya to district; final Ministry of Planning approval announced on the governorate's official site thiqar.gov.iq (~2019).
Former nahiya (of al-Rifa'i); became a district on 14 October 2018 per the ar.wikipedia Qada'a al-Nasr article; confirmed among the governorate's aqdia in 2026 press.
Elevated from nahiya of Nasiriyah to district; Ministry of Planning approval documented April 2019 (admin code 33141), governor's endorsement Sept 2019.
Elevated from nahiya of Suq al-Shuyukh to district; Ministry of Planning approval announced Aug 2019 (admin code 33151), retaining Nahiya al-Tar transferred from Suq al-Shuyukh (code 33152).

provinces.notes: Sources used: ar.wikipedia 'أقضية العراق' (current; lists 13 districts), ar.wikipedia 'محافظة ذي قار' (2022 admin table; 8 districts, mixed/outdated), individual ar.wikipedia district articles, thiqar.gov.iq official announcements (~2019 and 2026), nasiriaelc.com reports of IHEC/Ministry of Planning approvals (2018–2019), citypopulation.de (COSIT 2018 estimate snapshot), en.wikipedia 'Dhi Qar Governorate' and 'Districts of Iraq'. DISCREPANCIES: en.wikipedia lists only 6 districts and 'Districts of Iraq' only 5 — both reflect the pre-2014 structure and are outdated. citypopulation.de lists 10 (2018 COSIT snapshot): Ad-Dawayah, Al-Fuhud, Al-Islah, Al-Jibayish, An-Nasiriyah, Ar-Rifa'i, Ash-Shatrah, Qal'at Sikar, Sa'id Dakhil, Suq ash-Shuyukh — it misses al-Gharraf, al-Fajr, al-Nasr, al-Batha'a and Karmat Bani Sa'id. The 2022 ar.wiki admin table lists 8 (Nasiriyah, Shatrah, al-Rifa'i, Suq al-Shuyukh, al-Jibayish, al-Nasr, al-Fajr, al-Fuhud) and re-treats al-Islah, Sayyid Dakhil, al-Gharraf, Qal'at Sukkar and al-Dawaya as subdistricts, contradicting their 2014–2019 Ministry-approved district status. The current ar.wiki 'Aqdia al-Iraq' list (13) omits Sayyid Dakhil and al-Islah — almost certainly wiki incompleteness, as both are confirmed districts by official sources through 2026. One academic paper (~2024) still calls al-Fuhud a nahiya of al-Jibayish and Karmat Bani Sa'id a nahiya of Suq al-Shuyukh — outdated relative to the 2018/2019 upgrades. A proposed Qada'a al-Ukaikah (2019 planning document) could not be confirmed as finalized and is not listed. Subdistrict lists reflect the post-upgrade structure; single-unit new districts are reported with empty lists and explanatory notes.

districts.notes: Provincial capital district. Its former subdistrict Suwair was upgraded to a district (~2025).
Former subdistricts Majd and Najmi were upgraded to districts (Majd by Aug 2026, Najmi by mid-2026).
Upgraded from subdistrict to district before 2018 (already a district with a central subdistrict in citypopulation.de 2018 data). Its former subdistrict Hilal was upgraded to a district ~2025.
Upgraded from subdistrict of Rumaitha to district; listed as a district in ar.wikipedia's Muthanna admin table (mid-2026) and by the governor (Aug 2026).
Upgraded from subdistrict (of Warka) to district; Ministry of Planning approval reported by INA ~2025.
Upgraded from subdistrict of Samawah to district; Ministry of Planning approval reported by INA ~2025.

Upgraded from subdistrict of Rumaitha to district; named as a district by the governor of Muthanna (Aug 2026). Some older sources (governorate website muthana.gov.iq, ar.wikipedia's Rumaitha article) still list it as a Rumaitha subdistrict.

provinces.notes: Muthanna's district structure has expanded beyond the older 5-district layout (Samawah, Rumaitha, Khidhir, Salman, Warka). Four former subdistricts were upgraded to districts: Warka (already a district in citypopulation.de's 2018 data), Suwair and Hilal (Iraqi Ministry of Planning approval reported by Iraqi News Agency INA ~2025, cited in ar.wikipedia's Rumaitha District article), Najmi (listed as a district in ar.wikipedia's Muthanna admin table, mid-2026), and Majd (named as a district by Governor Muhannad al-Attabi, iraqpaper.com 2026-08-31). Current official structure: 9 districts + 3 subdistricts (Karama under Warka, Daraji under Khidhir, Busaiyah under Salman) = 12 units, matching the old 5+7 count. Discrepancies: ar.wikipedia's infobox says 8 districts/3 subdistricts and its admin table still lists Majd as Rumaitha's subdistrict (likely edited before the Majd upgrade); the governor's Aug-2026 statement lists 8 districts (incl. Majd) + 3 subdistricts = 11 units but omits Samawah district, presumably because that land-title event did not cover the provincial-center district; muthana.gov.iq still describes Majd as a Rumaitha subdistrict (stale). en.wikipedia 'Districts of Iraq' still lists only 4 Muthanna districts (Al-Khidhir, Al-Rumaitha, Al-Salman, Al-Samawa) - outdated; en.wikipedia 'Muthanna Governorate' has no district list. Confirmed: Afak, Diwaniya and Hamza belong to Qadisiyyah Governorate (per 'Districts of Iraq' and citypopulation.de) and are NOT in Muthanna. Each district's subdistrict list below includes its central subdistrict (same name as the district), following citypopulation.de's 'Central Subdistrict' convention and ar.wikipedia's admin table.

districts.notes: Awn stayed with Karbala District; per a 2009 council decision it was initially assigned to Al-Husseiniya District.
Also known as Tuwayrij (الطويريج).
Al-Rahhaliya listed on the governorate article; the census list shows only the district center.
Subdistrict list could not be verified; only agricultural مقاطعات (land plots) are documented. District confirmed by ar.wikipedia.org/wiki/قضاء_الحر.
Al-Taf (الطف / الجرية) confirmed under this district per ar.wikipedia.org/wiki/ناحية_الطف.

provinces.notes: 5 districts per Arabic Wikipedia (محافظة كربلاء). Al-Husseiniya upgraded from nahiya to district in 2009; Al-Hurr is also now a district. The census-based list (قائمة نواحي العراق) still shows only 3 districts and predates these upgrades.

districts.notes: Subdistrict Al-Awja confirmed by ar.wiki 'قضاء تكريت' ('يتبع للقضاء إدارياً ناحية العوجة'). No other nahiya found; مقاطعات Malha, Al-Zulaya, Awinat are agricultural sub-units (مقاطعات), not nahiyas.

ar.wiki 'قضاء سامراء': 'يضم ثلاث نواحي هي المعتصم والثرثار ودجلة'. Note: a 2026 news item cited on ar.wiki's Tikrit page reported an attempt to annex Tikrit-area مقاطعات (Malha, Al-Zulaya, Awinat) to ناحية دجلة; no completed change documented.

ar.wiki 'قضاء بلد' lists الإسحاقي and يثرب as administrative units of the district; ar.wiki Saladin Governorate page states الضلوعية is 'ناحية تتبع قضاء بلد'. Yathrib as a Balad subdistrict is also confirmed by a Jan-2021 IMPACT/REACH factsheet ('Yathreb Subdistrict of Balad District').
ar.wiki 'قضاء بيجي' ('المدن والنواحي' section): الصينية، الزوية، ناحية مكحول.

ar.wiki 'قضاء الدور': since 1987 the district has no nahiyas other than ناحية المركز (district-centre subdistrict); former subdistricts Hamrin (حمرين) and Abu Dilf (أبو دلف) were abolished in 1987. Subdistrict list therefore left empty (markaz-only district).
ar.wiki 'قضاء الشرقاط' lists نواحي آشور، السهل الأخضر، تلول الباج (with population/area table).

ar.wiki 'قضاء طوز خورماتو' lists الطوز (مركز القضاء)، سليمان بيك، ينكجة، آمرلي — but آمرلي was promoted to qada'a in January 2017 (ar.wiki 'آمرلي'), so it is listed here as a district instead of a Tuz subdistrict. Subdistricts retained: Sulaiman Bek, Yankjah. en.wiki uses the name 'Tooz District'.

Previously known as Al-Faris (الفارس) — en.wiki 'Dujail District' ('formerly, Al-Faris'); ar.wiki 'قضاء الدجيل' ('سابقا: قضاء الفارس'). This explains IOM DTM's 'Al-Fares' district listing. Verified subdistrict: Al-Sheikh Jamil (الشيخ جميل) — ar.wiki 'قضاء الدجيل' plus an IOP Conference Series study (2023) locating a site in 'Salah Al-Din Province, Al-Dujail District, Al-Sheikh Jamil District'. ar.wiki's Dujail page also claims ناحية الثرثار, but that conflicts with ar.wiki's Samarra page (which documents Al-Tharthar as a Samarra subdistrict with stats); excluded as likely error.

Verified as qada'a (ar.wiki 'قضاء العلم': 'قضاء العلم هو قضاء في محافظة صلاح الدين'). Previously associated with Tikrit district (infobox on the page lists القضاء: تكريت, reflecting its older status as ناحية العلم, created 1962, later upgraded). No nahiya list found on the page or elsewhere — only villages listed; subdistrict list left empty.

Verified as qada'a: ar.wiki 'آمرلي' ('المستوى الإداري: قضاء') states it was a nahiya of Tuz Khurmatu until January 2017, when it was promoted to district. Predominantly Turkmen (Turkman-speaking, Shia) population — not Kurdish. The page lists villages but no nahiyas; subdistrict list left empty.

provinces.notes: DISTRICT-COUNT DISCREPANCY: en.wikipedia.org ('Districts of Iraq' and 'Saladin Governorate') lists 8 districts, but Iraq's Central Statistical Organization (as published on citypopulation.de) lists 10. The two additions are Al-Alam (العلم) and Amirli (آمرلي), both verified as qada'a: ar.wikipedia's 'قضاء العلم' page explicitly calls Al-Alam a qada'a of Saladin (created as a nahiya in 1962, later upgraded), and the ar.wikipedia 'آمرلي' page states Amirli was promoted from nahiya to qada'a in January 2017 (it had been a subdistrict of Tuz Khurmatu). Both are therefore included here. IOM DTM reports list an 'Al-Fares' district — this is Dujail, which was previously known as Al-Faris (الفارس); confirmed by en.wiki 'Dujail District' ('formerly, Al-Faris') and ar.wiki 'قضاء الدجيل' ('سابقا: قضاء الفارس'). Al-Tharthar (الثرثار) naming conflict: ar.wiki's Dujail page claims Dujail includes 'ناحية الثرثار', but ar.wiki's Samarra page documents ناحية الثرثار (with 1997/2012 population and area stats) as a Samarra subdistrict; Dujail's claim appears erroneous, so Al-Tharthar is listed only under Samarra.

districts.notes: Provincial capital district. Subdistrict placement verified by COSIT/citypopulation 2018 estimates: the five subdistricts sum exactly to the district total (286,786 + 81,460 + 132,587 + 52,785 + 47,162 = 600,780). ar.wikipedia's قائمة نواحي العراق additionally lists خرنبات and الهويدر under Ba'quba; neither appears in COSIT's official subdistrict list, so both are excluded.

Includes Jadidat Al-Shat (جديدة الشط), a newer subdistrict confirmed as part of Al-Khalis District by ar.wikipedia's ناحية جديدة الشط article and present in the COSIT-based 2024 census subdistrict list. ar.wikipedia additionally lists ناحية الغالبية and ناحية المحمودية (الأسود) under Al-Khalis; neither appears in COSIT's official list, so both are excluded pending verification.
Subdistrict placement verified by COSIT/citypopulation 2018 estimates: 164,017 + 46,851 + 43,658 = 254,526 = district total.

Mandali and Qazaniya placement verified by COSIT/citypopulation 2018 estimates: 101,607 + 31,995 + 14,575 = 148,177 = district total. (ar.wikipedia's قائمة نواحي العراق lists كنعان here, but COSIT places Kan'an in Ba'quba District.)

Part of the disputed territories: de facto split between Diyala and Sulaymaniyah Governorate (KRG). The KRG-administered portion (Qoratu and Maydan subdistricts) is not part of the official Diyala structure. Officially (COSIT): Khanaqin central + Al-Saadiya subdistricts (87,731 + 50,808 = 138,539 = district total); Jalawla was split off as its own district. Kurdish names verified via en.wikipedia (Khanaqin city: خانەقین/Xaneqîn; district: قەزای خانەقین/Qezay Xaneqîn).

Elevated from a subdistrict of Khanaqin District to a separate seventh district (reflected in the current en.wikipedia district table; COSIT's 2018 data still listed Jalawla as a subdistrict of Khanaqin, population 93,685 = current district population). Single-subdistrict district.

Disputed territory: officially in Diyala per the federal government of Iraq, but de facto split — the town of Kifri and its central subdistrict are administered by the KRG as part of Sulaymaniyah Governorate (Garmian). The official Diyala portion consists of the Jabara and Qara Tapa subdistricts only (10,041 + 41,538 = 51,579 = district total per COSIT). Kurdish district name verified via en.wikipedia (قەزای کفری).

provinces.notes: Diyala Governorate (محافظة ديالى, IQ-DI) comprises 7 districts and 22 subdistricts per the official COSIT-based structure. Khanaqin and Kifri districts are part of the Disputed Territories claimed by the Kurdistan Regional Government: both are officially in Diyala per the federal government but are de facto split between Diyala and Sulaymaniyah Governorate (KRG). Jalwala was elevated from a subdistrict of Khanaqin to a separate seventh district (reflected in the current en.wikipedia district table).
